sentences.text: Eoconfuciusornis holds the distinction of being the oldest known bird to possess a beak.
This animal was slightly smaller than its relative Confuciusornis but shared a similar pointed, toothless beak.
Its plumage featured black feathers on the wing coverts, nape, and tail, with a dark spotted pattern on the secondary flight feathers.
Grey feathers covered its hindlimbs and head, while brown feathers adorned its throat.
The species Eoconfuciusornis zhengi was named and described by Fucheng Zhang, Zhou Zhonghe, and Michael Benton in 2008.
The holotype specimen — the specific example the species is based on — was discovered near Sichakou in Fengning, Hebei province.
Taxonomically, Eoconfuciusornis is classified within the family Confuciusornithidae.
This extinct bird-like animal lived 131 million years ago in the Early Cretaceous period of China.
The genus existed during the Hauterivian to Barremian stages, spanning from 132.6 to 121.4 million years ago.
